body:
## Idea

When the user picks a folder via fzt-picker (e.g. the \`explore\` flow from homepage), the choice is useful context — the next time they pick, they probably want recent paths at the top.

Today each picker invocation is stateless: it shows the filesystem root and forces the user to drill in every time. For common workflows (open-in-explorer, code-in-folder, etc.), recent paths would cut navigation dramatically.

## Proposal

- Persist a list of recently-picked paths (local file, maybe \`%LOCALAPPDATA%\fzt-picker\recent.yaml\`)
- On launch, show a "recent" pseudo-folder at the top of the tree with the last N picks
- When the user picks something, prepend to the list (dedupe, cap at N)

## Open design questions

- N = 10? 20?
- Per-context scoping? Explorer-opens vs code-opens separate lists? Or one global?
- TTL — drop paths not touched in 30/90 days?
- Respect deleted-path invalidation (prune entries where the path no longer exists on disk)?

## Related

Surfaced during work on [my-homepage#21](https://github.com/nelsong6/my-homepage/issues/21) — picker returning a path that gets handed to explorer.exe. Recent list would make that flow materially faster.
title: Surface a 'recent paths' / history list for picked folders
